lead: `holes.py`'s per-item refusal sites are the file's *catch-all* panics, so an item can read "N sites standing" after the feature runs.
body: `lower_expr`'s and `emit_binop`'s "got {other:?}" arms are attributed to whatever item anchors their file and will still be there when the last hole closes. The tool ranks *candidates*; the ground truth is four lines in a scratch `.agent-tmp/*.nvs` and one `nvs run`, and `holes.py --cases` is the half that does not lie — a named case either exists on disk or does not.
